title: Violin in New Orleans dance bands
summary: Violins played lead in dance orchestras, with clarinet central in Dixieland groups; some improvised.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: Most of the machines now are being made this way to... Oh. Turn it over and the car is only on half of the tape and the upper half will be taken up. Anything else about the dance music? What kind of bands? They always had a violin, did they in those days, I understand?
Well, I... In the later years, I took up saxophone.
I mean, the New Orleans bands, did they always use a violin? The violin and the dance bands?
No. No. No. Not as much as the clarinet because... Having... More or less on the Dixon Land idea, there was always that clarinet.
That's what I always thought the violin didn't fit in so well. Yes. Yes.
They still tell me sometimes... But we did have orchestras. Oh, and a number of orchestras. They used violins in those days much more... Dance officers than we do now.
What kind of a part, if they played in more or less Dixieland band, in that, say, six or seven piece group, what kind of a part would the violin play?
Always, of course, the lead. Just stick to the lead. You didn't... Oh, all right.
They didn't try to get fancy and run...
Well, yes, we had boys there who were pretty clever with that sort of thing. You mean improvisation? Yes, improvisation. Yeah.
